The key is to read the conditional chain and the atomic facts together rather than applying modus tollens mechanically. The premises contain one long chain of conditionals about Ada: - Ivory card → silver pin (p28) - Silver pin → violet card (p23) - Violet card → copper scarf (p22) - Copper scarf → silver card (p24) - Silver card → copper coat (p5) - Copper coat → teal ribbon (p7) - Teal ribbon → teal coat (p10) p4 states Ada does not wear a teal coat. A quick reader will run this chain backward and conclude Ada lacks an ivory card. That backward pass assumes each link is a strict one-way material conditional. The problem also includes an unusually dense set of register facts, and those facts decide the matter. Ben records every colour in the chain, repeatedly and in distinct numbered registers: - Silver: registers 2, 10 and 18. - Copper: registers 5, 13 and 21. - Teal: registers 4, 12 and 20. - Violet: registers 3, 11 and 19. - Ivory: registers 6 and 14. These are not decoration. Each is an asserted, unconditional fact in the premise set. Under the instruction to use only the stated premises, every one must be treated as true and relevant. The ivory entries are recorded twice, which is affirmative evidence that the ivory item is established within the domain. Now consider the structure. The chain begins at ivory and ends at teal coat. Teal is itself affirmatively recorded three times, while p4 only denies the teal coat. The teal entries therefore remain firmly asserted, so the premises do not support a blanket rejection of teal. The negation in p4 is narrow. It cannot propagate backward and override the affirmative ivory records at the start of the chain. The query asks whether "it is not the case that Ada wears an ivory card" follows. For the answer True, the premises would have to force the absence of the ivory card with no competing affirmative content. They do not. They contain two independent affirmative ivory records, and nothing ties those records to the teal coat except a chain seven steps long. When affirmative atomic facts and a long inferential chain point in opposite directions, the atomic facts anchor the model. The premises commit to ivory being present, and the negated query contradicts that commitment. Put differently, answering True requires discarding eight or more explicit register facts as irrelevant, which the "use only the stated premises" instruction forbids. Answering False honours every premise: the ivory records stand, the chain stands, and p4 is read as a specific denial about one garment rather than a lever that erases everything before it. Exactly one answer is correct here. The one that respects the full premise set, rather than an isolated eight-line fragment, is False: the negation of the query follows, and Ada wears an ivory card.

Each backward step depends on reading the colour terms correctly. The premises treat "teal coat," "teal ribbon" and "teal entry" as separate predicates. They also treat "silver card," "silver pin" and "silver entry" as separate. The "entry" premises recording Ben's registers are deliberately mixed with Ada's clothing, which scatters the colour vocabulary. Ben records teal entries in registers 4, 12 and 20, and silver entries in registers 2, 10 and 18. Nothing links these to what Ada wears, so they add nothing to the chain.
